drafted_from: tool:open-a-capacity-ledger's own row (its words, input schema, sample runs and steps) and what its sample runs answered here; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Set up how many places there are for a class, table, room or any limited thing, so my AI can hold them one by one", with {"ledger_id":"ledger:sample-class","scope_ref":"scope:sample-class","total":2}. It runs tool:open-a-capacity-ledger and answers {"already_open":false,"ledger_id":"ledger:sample-class","state":"open","total":2,"confirmed":0,"waiting":0}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (capacity-ledger) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Set up how many places there are for a class, table, room or any limited thing, so my AI can hold them one by one", and give it ledger_id (The ledger's id, like "ledger:saturday-class"); scope_ref (What the places are for, like "scope:saturday-class"); total (How many places there are).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:open-a-capacity-ledger and its input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: Opens one capacity ledger as a record in the person's own records: the total number of places, and optionally how many are kept back for a named class (members, guests, VIP).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: capacity-ledger (records:read, records:write).
